title: Aniimo Eggs, Breeding and Homeland Explained | Full Guide | Aniimo Guide
description: A complete Aniimo guide to eggs, the Hatchinator, potential, Aniipods and the Homeland: how to get new Aniimo, hatch them and put them to work.

sections.heading: Two systems that power your whole team
sections.script: If you play Aniimo, the open world creature game from Pawprint Studio, two systems quietly decide how strong your team becomes: eggs and the Homeland. Eggs are how you grow your collection and chase better Aniimo, with higher potential and rare mutations. The Homeland is your personal base, where Aniimo hatch, work and keep your whole adventure running while you explore. In this guide we explain how breeding works in Aniimo, where eggs come from, how the Hatchinator hatches them, what the special Aniipods really do, and how to unlock and run your Homeland step by step. A quick note: the game changes with patches, so check the in-game menus if a number looks different for you.

sections.heading: Breeding means eggs
sections.script: First, let's clear up a common question. In Aniimo, the way to get new Aniimo through hatching is not to pair two creatures together. Instead, the game is built around eggs. You find or earn an egg, put it in an incubator, wait, and when it is ready, you meet a brand new Aniimo. Every egg carries labels that tell you something about what is inside, such as an element or a guaranteed quality, so reading those labels before you start incubating is a smart habit. Guides also point out that some eggs can only be hatched at certain machines, which we will cover in a moment. Think of eggs as the heart of breeding in this game.

sections.heading: Where eggs come from
sections.script: There are several ways to collect eggs. Nests in the open world hold eggs, and they are often placed high up or in places that make you work for them. Daily Activities reward you with eggs when you complete the listed tasks, and the Companion Handbook, which is the battle pass, gives eggs at certain level milestones. Elite Training can reward special eggs as well. Later in the game, the Operation Egg Heist mode is another big source, with rarer eggs as the prize. Guides also mention that sending your RV on expeditions from the Homeland can bring back rare eggs. So even on a quiet day, there is always some way to add another egg to your collection.

sections.heading: The Hatchinator
sections.script: Eggs are hatched in a machine called the Hatchinator. There are two kinds of locations: an Outpost Hatchinator out in the world, and a Hatchinator in your own Homeland. They work in much the same way, with three slots each. The middle slot only accepts higher quality eggs, so you often cannot run all three at once with ordinary eggs. Hatching runs in real time, and the timer keeps going even while you are offline, so it is a good idea to fill your slots before you log off. A few special eggs can only be hatched at an Outpost machine, so read the item text when an egg will not go into your home machine.

sections.heading: How to hatch an egg
sections.script: The steps are simple. Walk up to the Hatchinator and press the interaction prompt, then choose Start Hatching and pick an egg. Place it in a free slot and confirm. Now wait for the timer. When the slot shows an exclamation mark, the egg is ready: select it, choose an Aniipod, and pet the egg to begin the reveal. Finally, review the result and press Claim. Because hatching runs in real time, it helps to plan your sessions around the timers, starting long eggs before you log off and short ones when you are about to play.

sections.heading: Potential and egg types
sections.script: Every Aniimo has a potential, which decides how strong its attributes can ultimately become, and egg potential is set before the creature hatches. This is why egg types matter. An Incredible Egg guarantees Elite potential or higher, and it takes about two hours and thirty minutes to hatch. Daily Activity quests are a reliable source of Incredible Eggs. A Sparkling Egg guarantees the Sparkling mutation, takes about five hours, and can come from Elite Training, the Stamp Shop or Catch Completion rewards. Perfect potential is the best result you can get, and some eggs are made to guarantee it. If you are chasing a strong main team, aim for these better egg types first.

sections.heading: Aniipods that really matter
sections.script: When you hatch, the game lets you pick an Aniipod, and this is where many players waste resources. Guides agree that only two Aniipods change the result of a hatch: the Aniipod Ultra and the Sparkling Cube. Aniipod Ultra sets the potential to at least Elite, while the Sparkling Cube is the prismatic rarity one that is used to chase rare variants. All other Aniipods, such as the standard ones, are tools for catching wild Aniimo and do nothing for hatching. The advice is to use an Ultra only when the egg would otherwise end up lower than Elite, so an Incredible Egg, which already guarantees Elite, does not need one.

sections.heading: Unlocking your Homeland
sections.script: Now to the Homeland. You unlock it at character level twenty by starting the introductory RV mission. A character named Fannie gives you the RV, and you register it at the park board, then step through the portal inside it to reach your own home. The first tutorial has you plant and harvest your first wheat, and you can sell it at the Home Co-op Store. Home Coins are the main Homeland currency, and you spend them on RV upgrades, plots and facility upgrades. Each RV level adds more plots and more room for your Aniimo, and improves output, so upgrading the RV is the main way to grow your base over time.

sections.heading: Facilities and workers
sections.script: The Homeland works in a loop. Unlock a plot, place a facility from the Build menu, check which ability it asks for, and assign Aniimo workers with a matching Homeland ability. How fast a facility finishes its orders depends on those abilities and their levels rather than on combat stats, and ability levels run from one to four. Level four is rare, and only Prismana forms can reach it. Guides recommend favoring Aniimo with several Homeland abilities, because one creature can then staff more kinds of facilities. Keep in mind that an Aniimo working at a facility cannot fight, so catching a duplicate lets one species farm while the other joins your team.

sections.heading: Food, rest and friends
sections.script: Your workers need care. Cooked food goes into a shared food supply, and workers draw from it when their energy runs low, but if it runs dry they stop working. A Nimbus Bed gives them a place to recover, so it is one of the first facilities to build. Crops and cooked food run on timers that continue while you are offline, so stock your seeds and queue your jobs before you log off. Friends can help your eggs too: a friend who visits your Homeland and pets an incubating egg takes ten minutes off its timer. Good early priorities are mining piles, basic woodland nodes, crops and worker recovery.

sections.heading: What is your egg luck
sections.script: That is the full loop: collect eggs, hatch them in the Hatchinator, pick the right Aniipod, and let your Homeland run in the background. Now we want to hear from you. Have you hatched a Sparkling or Perfect Aniimo yet? Which Aniimo do you want to put to work in your Homeland? And what is your favorite way to find eggs? Tell us in the comments. If this guide helped, like the video and subscribe for more Aniimo guides, and we will see you in the next one. Happy hatching, Pathfinder.
